title: Finite discrete internal constructibility has a classical etale model
statement: Let $T$ be a finite discrete commutative ring and $Z$ a Noetherian scheme (quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] and locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]). Put $T_Z^c=p_Z^*\underline T$ [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Use the explicitly constructed exact equivalence $E_Z$ from ordinary $T$-module sheaves on $Z_{\mathrm{proét}}$ to internal $T_Z^c$-modules [def-weil-pbc-common-finite-discrete-encoding], with its finite-discrete constant-ring identification. Let $\nu_Z:Z_{\mathrm{proét}}\to Z_{\mathrm{ét}}$ be site comparison [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. For $K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(T_Z^c))$ [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories], the following are equivalent: (i) $K$ is bounded constructible in the general ring-object, stratified locally finitely presented sense [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible]; (ii) there is a bounded complex $L$ with classical constructible cohomology on $Z_{\mathrm{ét}}$, an object of $D(Z_{\mathrm{ét}},T)$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], and an isomorphism $K\cong E_Z\nu_Z^*L$ in that ordinary derived category. Classical constructible means locally on affine opens a finite constructible locally closed partition makes each cohomology sheaf locally constant with finite $T$-module values [sk-thm-pe-constructible-comparison]. The zero ring is allowed, and no Tor amplitude is imposed.

source.place: §5.1 and §5.4, with explicit finite-discrete encoding; no direct-image finiteness is asserted

proof.text: Write $E=E_Z$ and $F=E^{-1}$ for the explicitly specified common encoding, with its fixed finite-discrete coefficient identification. These are additive exact equivalences. Apply the exact-functor localization construction to both: their termwise unit and counit descend to inverse derived isomorphisms. For either $G=E,F$, exact cohomology comparison gives $H^q(D(G)C)\cong G(H^q(C))$. Thus $D(E)$ and $D(F)$ preserve and reflect every cohomological vanishing interval, since an equivalence preserves and reflects the zero object. Set $J=D(F)K$. In what follows the expression $E\nu_Z^*L$ in the statement means the termwise induced derived functor $D(E)D(\nu_Z^*)L$ in the ordinary, uncompleted derived category.

source.place: Tag 015F, lemma-right-derived-exact-functor; homology.tex Tag 010N, lemma-exact-functor; agent application to the common encoding

proof.text: For later use, every finite $T$-module $P$ is finitely presented. Indeed $T^{(P)}\to P$, sending the basis vector indexed by $p$ to $p$, is surjective; its kernel $N$ is a finite set because $T$ and $P$ are finite. The map $T^{(N)}\to T^{(P)}$ sending the basis vector indexed by $n$ to $n$ has image that kernel. Both ranks are finite. Conversely a finitely presented $T$-module is a quotient of a finite power of the finite set $T$, hence finite. The same reasoning says that $T$ is Noetherian: every ideal is generated by its finite underlying set. These arguments include $T=0$ and do not say that a finite module is projective.

source.place: Agent finite-module calculation for finite-discrete coefficients; the finite-presentation definition

proof.text: Assume (i). The definition of bounded constructibility provides integers $a\le b$ with $H^q(K)=0$ outside $[a,b]$ and an internal finite-stratification constructibility witness for every $H^q(K)$. Apply finite-discrete constructible encoding to each such sheaf. Its statement gives that $F(H^q(K))$ has a global finite stratification with pro-étale covers by finite constant $T$-modules. Step 1 identifies this sheaf with $H^q(J)$ and preserves the bounds. The fixed-module constructible-origin equivalence now supplies, for each $q$, a globally constructible étale $T$-module sheaf $A_q$ and an isomorphism $\nu_Z^*A_q\cong H^q(J)$. All these applications allow a finite commutative ring with no characteristic assumption.

source.place: Tag 09AK, lemma-compare-constructible; finite-discrete sectionwise encoding as specified in the item

proof.text: Apply bounded fixed-module constructible origin to $J$ and the $A_q$ of step 3. It gives a bounded étale derived object $L$ with globally constructible cohomology and $J\cong D(\nu_Z^*)L$. Its global stratifications restrict to affine opens, so its cohomology is classical constructible in the statement's affine-local sense. If a literally bounded cochain representative is desired, choose its finite cohomological interval and apply the bounded-representative lemma; replacing $L$ by this representative preserves its cohomology and the displayed isomorphism. Apply $D(E)$ and compose with its derived counit from step 1 to obtain $K\cong D(E)D(\nu_Z^*)L$. This proves (ii).

source.place: Tag 09AL, lemma-compare-constructible-derived, and Tag 099V, lemma-compare-derived; bounded representative: Mathlib DerivedCategory.exists_iso_Q_obj_of_isGE_of_isLE

proof.text: Conversely assume (ii). Since Z is quasi-compact and locally Noetherian, it is Noetherian. Apply the existing source theorem Scheme.IsConstructibleSheaf.of_iSup_eq_top to H^q(L) and the cover by all affine opens. The hypothesis gives constructibility of each restriction, so this theorem provides a global finite stratification. On each stratum the etale sheaf is finite locally constant. Choose an etale cover trivializing it; discard empty members, so the finite-sheaf condition implies that every constant module value is finite. This etale cover is also pro-etale. Comparison inverse image commutes with these restrictions and takes constant sheaves to constant sheaves. Its existing exact functor API identifies its application to H^q(L) with H^q(D(nu_Z^*)Q(L)).

proof.text: Let $G$ be any ordinary pro-étale module sheaf with one of the finite-model stratifications just obtained. On each stratum and each member $U$ of its trivializing cover, write $G|_U\cong\underline P_U$ with $P$ finite. Restriction compatibility for the common encoding identifies $(E_ZG)|_U$ with $E_U(\underline P_U)$, including the pulled-back coefficient identification. Sheafify the finite presentation of $P$ from step 2; the exact constant-module functor gives $\underline T_U^m\to\underline T_U^n\to\underline P_U\to0$. Applying the exact equivalence $E_U$ preserves this cokernel and the finite sums. Its image of the rank-one free module is the regular $T_U^c$-module: under the encoding's underlying-abelian-sheaf isomorphism, maps out of either object correspond naturally to global sections of the underlying sheaf, by evaluating a module map at $1$; these bijections identify the two rank-one representing objects. Hence $E_U(\underline P_U)$ is a cokernel of $(T_U^c)^m\to(T_U^c)^n$. By the definitions of finite presentation, local finite presentation and constructibility, $E_ZG$ is internally constructible, with the same finite stratification and covering families. In Lean the ordinary constant-sheaf functor preserves finite colimits, so its cokernel comparison suffices; no separate derived constant-module functor is used. The existing encoded finite-free isomorphism identifies finite free internal modules with constant finite sums of G of the regular scalar module. The scalar isomorphism G(R_regular) ≅ R is constructed by the natural hom-set equivalence given by evaluation at one and hG, followed by fully faithful coyoneda. Finite-presentation transport along coefficient isomorphisms uses the existing pullback module API.

source.place: Definition of constructibility and local finite presentation; constant module sheafification: sites-modules.tex Tags 03CY, lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules, and 093I, section-constant; agent finite-presentation calculation

proof.text: Apply step 6 to $G=\nu_Z^*H^q(L)$ for every $q$. Steps 1 and 5 identify its encoding with $H^q(D(E)D(\nu_Z^*)L)$. Thus all cohomology sheaves of that complex are internally constructible. Choose the cohomological bounds of $L$; the two exact functors preserve their zero cohomology outside those bounds. Finally the isomorphism in (ii) induces isomorphisms of cohomology sheaves with those of $K$. Compose the finite-presentation witnesses with these isomorphisms, so the same constructibility and zero-cohomology conditions hold for $K$. This is precisely (i) by the definition of bounded constructibility. Neither direction imposed a Tor-amplitude bound.
